China scholarships

Scholarships

Funding your study in China, end to end.

China funds more international students than almost any country on earth. The list of awards is long, the eligibility is messy, and the deadlines sneak up. This page is the field guide — every major scholarship, what it covers, who qualifies, and when to apply.

The five scholarships worth your time

Most students should apply to two or three of these. CSC is the headline, but provincial and university awards are easier to win and often cover the same tuition.

CSC

Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC)

CoverageCoverage depends on the specific award; check tuition, accommodation, stipend and insurance in its notice

EligibilityDegree, age, citizenship, language and academic requirements depend on the current scheme. Check undergraduate CSCA requirements separately from postgraduate eligibility.

Typical deadlineUse the current university or nominating authority’s deadline
Read the full CSC guide on SICA →

CIS

International Chinese Language Teachers Scholarship

CoverageTuition · housing · monthly stipend (CNY 2,500–3,000) · insurance

EligibilityA separate language-education scholarship route. Consult CLEC’s current guidelines for HSK, HSKK, degree and recommending-institution requirements.

Typical deadlineCheck the current CLEC and host-institution notices
Browse Confucius Institute programs →

PGS

Provincial Government Scholarships

CoverageCoverage and selection vary by the province or city and award

EligibilityCheck the education authority and receiving university for an award that applies to your degree, citizenship and intake.

Typical deadlineCheck the specific provincial or university notice
See provincial awards by region →

USS

University-specific scholarships

CoverageTuition reduction (partial or full); some include housing. Awarded on merit after admission.

EligibilityCheck each university’s current eligibility, selection process and whether a separate scholarship application is required.

Typical deadlineMay require a separate application; confirm with the university
Compare top universities and their awards →

Bilateral

Bilateral & exchange-country programs

CoverageFunding depends on the agreement and the named scholarship scheme

EligibilityCheck the current notice from the responsible embassy, ministry or university for eligibility and nomination instructions.

Typical deadlineCheck the responsible nominating authority’s current notice

How CSCA fits your application

CSCA results can be part of an undergraduate application. The receiving program and scholarship provider determine the exact requirements; no score guarantees funding.

Check the current undergraduate admission notice for your required subjects, paper languages and score-report deadline. A high-school qualification, language evidence and an exam result may all be needed.

We do not publish universal score cutoffs or admission probabilities. A practice percentage describes that question set; it cannot determine whether a university or scholarship committee will accept you.

Use our free topic practice, worked explanations, timed mocks and spaced-repetition review to identify gaps in your preparation.

Common questions

Do I need to take the CSCA to apply for a Chinese scholarship?
Check the current notice for the exact degree, teaching language and scholarship. CSCA can be required for undergraduate applications, including English-taught programs. Do not assume a waiver or that a school qualification substitutes for the test.
What is the difference between the CSC scholarship and a university scholarship?
Chinese Government Scholarships and university-funded awards have different funding sources and selection rules. Compare the coverage, separate application steps and restrictions on holding multiple awards in the actual notices.
Can I apply for a Chinese scholarship without a Chinese language background?
Some programs are taught in English, but language evidence and any funded preparatory study depend on the scheme. Check the university’s exact language requirements and the scholarship’s coverage before applying.
How competitive are Chinese scholarships?
Competition depends on the scheme and applicant pool. We do not have a representative dataset that supports a universal competitive CSCA score or funding probability. Use published eligibility and selection criteria for the specific award.
When should I start preparing my scholarship application?
Start early enough to gather documents, complete any required tests and meet each published deadline. University, embassy nomination and scholarship deadlines can differ; keep a separate calendar for each.
